rv.q: It is not the clarity of delivery, but the underplaying of plot points that leaves this mighty drama feel more brittle than tragic.
Den Hertog has given a Lear not just of our age but one to live long in the memory, in essence, for ages yet to come.
Consistently strong performances in Pitlochry Festival Theatre’s staging of Shakespeare’s tragedy, led by Maureen Beattie
Ultimately, fine as Beattie is in the title role, it’s as an ensemble achievement that this Lear is remarkable, and it’s a worthy vehicle for Shakespeare’s return to Pitlochry.
Understandably, he throws a lot at it; understandably, it doesn't all work.
This is an ambitious, unsettling production which embraces both the traditional and modern, creating a Lear that feels both timeless and deeply relevant to the world of today.
